headings.text: What actually matters in a 7 kg fully automatic washing machine

cta.headline: Match the machine to your laundry
cta.sub: Front load saves detergent and water; top load is gentler on mixed loads and faster for daily washes.

faq.q: Is 7 kg enough for a family of four?
faq.a: Yes, 7 kg is the most popular size for Indian families of 3 to 5. It handles daily loads of mixed clothes and a weekly bedsheet-and-towel cycle comfortably. Move to 8 or 9 kg only if you frequently wash curtains, blankets or king-size comforters.

faq.q: Front load or top load -- which is better?
faq.a: Front load machines use less water and detergent, give gentler wash, and usually spin faster. Top load machines are easier to load, faster for single washes, and cheaper. Pick front load if you wash often and value water savings; pick top load for convenience and shorter cycle times.

faq.q: What is a 5-star rating washing machine?
faq.a: BEE 5-star rating means the machine uses less electricity per kg of laundry than lower-rated models. The upfront saving is usually Rs 2,000 to Rs 5,000, and you recover it in 3 to 4 years of regular use through lower bills.

faq.q: Do washing machines need a stabilizer?
faq.a: Most current machines have built-in voltage protection that handles 150 to 270 V. A separate stabilizer is needed only in areas with persistent low voltage, frequent power cuts, or rural supply that drops below 150 V.

faq.q: How long does a washing machine last?
faq.a: A well-maintained fully automatic washing machine lasts 8 to 12 years. Direct-drive motors (used by LG and Samsung premium models) typically outlast belt-drive motors. Clean the drum and detergent drawer monthly to extend life.
